title: Tools that build tools, under governance
subtitle: A generator that lets agents add new capabilities to the estate, inside a sandbox, callable only after a human restart

stats.label: function crates in the estate carry the generator's fingerprints
per function: eight framework, six sandboxed
places written in one rollback-protected transaction per generation

lede: My agents could call tools and could not add one. Every new capability meant a human wiring a crate into the gateway, the orchestrator and the result path by hand. I built a generator, exposed as a tool, that lets an agent author a new function for the estate. The generated code runs in a sandbox that sees only a capability-bounded context, cannot open its own connections or write the database directly, and runs only after a human rebuilds and restarts the gateway. AI-written processing code, given a database handle, will build unsafe queries, write tables it should not, and open connections nobody audits.
quote: Self-extending systems are where safety usually goes to die.
evidence: Tool synthesis and governed API integration: a generator, itself an MCP tool, that lets an AI agent author a new function, with 7 of 14 function crates in the estate carrying its fingerprints.
Sandboxing generated code: 14 files per function, eight framework files locked and six in a sandbox that reads through a schema resolver and writes only through the governed queue.
Transactional code generation: 4 places written in one rollback-protected transaction per generation, with a symmetric delete and link-time registration so nothing is half-registered.
Human-in-the-loop control for AI agents: a generated function runs only after a human rebuilds and restarts the gateway.
Self-audit and redesign: a first version that passed its own fifteen-point check but generated code that did not compile, rebuilt with inverted ownership instead of patched.
author: Corey James
